regime.read: Regime level GREEN with VIX 17.3: calm on the index. Under the surface the tape is defensive: the leading sectors are Healthcare, Staples and Energy, Technology is graded AVOID and sits in WEAKENING/DEEPENING, and the S&P is -0.56% over 20 days and +2.9% over 63 days. Calm index plus defensive leadership reads as a rotation market, not a risk-on trend.
regime.momentum_caveat: Hurst and trend fields are NOT in my packet, so I cannot call TREND vs MEAN_REVERT; the momentum caveat cannot be confirmed either way. On what is served, leadership is defensive and young (Healthcare DEPLOY for 1 session, Staples and Energy 'Momentum Fading - Hold, Don't Add'), growth themes are broadly LAGGING/DEEPENING, and the index is flat over 20 days. A momentum book is fishing in a small, defensive pond. Treat every momentum nomination as working against a non-trending index.

cross_asset.value: roc5 -0.41 / roc20 +1.47, below 20d SMA, direction FALLING
cross_asset.read: Short-term softening after a 20-day rise. A falling dollar normally helps risk, but here it is not lifting copper or gold, so it is not reflationary. Runner-up scenario (dollar squeeze) is not confirmed while price is below the 20d SMA.

cross_asset.value: roc5 +2.25 / roc20 -1.98, above 20d SMA, direction RISING
cross_asset.read: Bonds bid this week: falling yields. Together with weak copper this looks like a growth scare bid, not an easing tailwind for risk.

cross_asset.value: roc5 -0.34 / roc20 -2.34, below 20d SMA; HY-minus-Treasury spread -2.59
cross_asset.read: Credit is lagging Treasuries and sits below its 20d trend. Credit is softening while equities are calm. This is the most important warning on the board: credit usually turns first.

cross_asset.value: oil roc5 +4.91 RISING; copper roc5 -1.73 FALLING; gold roc5 -1.05 FALLING; copper/gold roc5 -0.68 (roc20 +1.64)
cross_asset.read: Oil up while copper falls is the stagflation mix: input costs rising and growth slowing. The 5-day copper/gold tilt is toward deflation and risk-off, but it is still positive over 20 days, so the turn is fresh, not established.
Large caps are beating small caps by 3.4 points over 20 days. Risk appetite has not reached the small end.

risk_call: Leaning risk-off. Bonds are bid, credit is soft, copper is weak and leadership is defensive. The calm VIX and a GREEN regime level argue against outright risk-off, so this is a defensive tilt, not a liquidation call.

rotation.read: Tailwind. LEADING/ENTERING (RS 102.53, mom 109.02), macro headwind 0.0, entry gate PASS. Just upgraded to DEPLOY; the Biotech theme is LEADING with 100% breadth and MedTech is IMPROVING.
Macro TAILWIND (+0.54 each). Staples LEADING/ENTERING; Utilities IMPROVING but EXITING. Classic defensive bid, consistent with bonds rising.

LEADING/DEEPENING (RS 106.34) with oil rising, but trend state is 'Fading - Hold, Don't Add' (roc5 1.15 vs roc20 10.02). The sub-themes disagree with the sector: Oil Services, Midstream and Nuclear are all LAGGING. Late and narrow.

IMPROVING/ENTERING but macro CAUTION (-0.40). Insurance LEADING with 90% breadth; Big Banks IMPROVING; Fintech and Crypto LAGGING/DEEPENING. Defensive financials are working, rate-sensitive and speculative ones are not.

Headwind. Technology AVOID, WEAKENING/DEEPENING, macro headwind -0.90. Semis (breadth 6.7%), Chip Equipment (0%), AI Infrastructure, Quantum, Space and Crypto are all LAGGING. Mag7 is WEAKENING with a bearish rising wedge forming. The exception is Enterprise Software: LEADING/DEEPENING, roc20 +11.34, breadth 76.2%. But its parent sector is AVOID, which caps the grade.

Macro HEADWIND (-0.94 to -1.06). Industrials and Comm Services are entry-BLOCKED (LAGGING), and Infra Power has a triggered bearish head-and-shoulders. Discretionary is IMPROVING but EXITING. Materials is IMPROVING, but Critical Minerals, Gold Miners and Agri are LAGGING.
Homebuilders and REITs are IMPROVING (breadth 71.4%), and Payments is IMPROVING with 100% breadth. These are early beneficiaries if bonds keep rising. They are not leaders yet.

breadth.read: Mixed and narrow by my proxies. Large caps lead small caps by 3.42 over 20 days, and macro_weather labels the tape 'narrow'. Sector dispersion: 3 of 11 sectors LEADING (all defensive or late-cycle), 5 IMPROVING, 2 LAGGING and Technology WEAKENING. Most growth themes have breadth below 25%. Crown's 'broadening' label is 2 days old, and its own 5d/20d breadth is up inside a -3.59% 60-day decline. That is a short-term turn, not yet a durable broadening.
breadth.label: proxy

lean_18m: Bonds bid, credit soft, copper falling, oil rising: the mix of a growth slowdown with sticky input costs. Over 18 months I lean toward defensive quality and away from capex/AI-beta until credit and copper/gold confirm. If they do, the lean flips quickly.
sizing_rationale: Credit is softening while bonds rally, growth leadership is broken, dealer gamma is negative with the S&P index within 1% of the flip, and leadership is defensive and young. Hurst is unavailable to confirm a trend. A calm VIX keeps this at light rather than defensive cash.

agrees_on: Vol stress is leaving: index VIX is calm at 17.3, and I see no panic in cross-asset either
Dispersion regime: wide gaps between sectors and themes (Enterprise Software +11.34 vs Crypto -32.37 over 20 days) and low implied correlation are consistent with my rotation read
Negative dealer gamma, with the S&P index 0.77% from the flip: swings can run larger than the macro news justifies, which supports light sizing
Breadth regime is young and sits inside a 60-day decline; not yet durable
differs_on: Crown calls breadth 'broadening'. My proxies say narrow: large caps beat small caps by 3.42 over 20 days, and small caps are FALLING in macro_weather. Crown's own small-cap trend-fund flip (+1.49% away) has not been crossed. I would not call broadening until small caps confirm
Crown's data points give no read on credit. I weight HY underperforming Treasuries (spread -2.59, HY below its 20d SMA) as a leading risk-off warning that a calm VIX does not cancel
Runner-up scenario DOLLAR_SQUEEZE: the dollar is falling over 5 days and sits below its 20d SMA, so my cross-asset read does not support a squeeze today

what_would_change_it: Credit recovers above its 20d SMA and the HY-Treasury gap narrows: removes the main risk-off warning; tone moves to normal
Copper/gold turns back up over 5 days alongside a rising copper: reflation, and the lean rotates back toward cyclicals and materials
Small caps outperform large caps (spread turns negative) and the small-cap trend-fund flip is crossed: confirms Crown's broadening; tone moves to normal
Technology regains IMPROVING/LEADING with semis breadth recovering above 50%: growth leadership returns, which momentum needs
the S&P index loses the dealer flip and then the put wall in a negative-gamma tape while credit weakens further: move to defensive or cut further
Oil keeps rising while bonds sell off (yields up): stagflation becomes a rates problem and the defensive bond-proxy bid fails
